title: Regional hedging and probabilistic load-shedding for tail-latency protection
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem statement: We observe sporadic tail-latency spikes (> p99) in production for routes that fan out to Redis and Kafka during regional load bursts. These spikes cause request pile-up at the runtime which blows connection pools and cascades into DB timeouts and user-visible errors. Goal: implement a combined approach of regional hedging, adaptive circuit breakers, and probabilistic load-shedding to protect SLOs and maintain graceful degradation.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end latency p99 for API route /v1/chat should be <= 750ms under 99th percentile baseline load within 3 weeks of rollout
Circuit breaker prevents >90% of downstream-induced tail failures by tripping before pool exhaustion in staging and production experiments
Probabilistic load-shedding reduces incoming QPS to degraded backends by at least 40% during simulated overload while maintaining high-priority requests
Runbook with triage steps and automated fallback triggers added to on-call rotation; playbook validated in chaos experiment
implementation_notes:
Design summary:
1) Hedging: send a lightweight hedged read to secondary region if primary backend latency exceeds p95_threshold (configurable per-route). Hedged requests are capped to X% of traffic and use stale-read mode for Redis where acceptable. We will implement hedging in the request pipeline after the KV cache lookup to avoid duplicating expensive generation work.
2) Connection pool protection: introduce bounded wait queues with hard timeouts and a probabilistic early drop ('ticketing') when queue depth exceeds soft_limit. Increase connection pool observability: per-backend metrics for active, idle, queued, waits, and queue_overflow.
3) Circuit breakers: stateful breakers with sliding-window failure rate + queue-saturation signal. States: CLOSED -> OPEN (with exponentially backed-off half-open probes) -> HALF-OPEN. Tripping conditions include: failure_rate > 20% OR average queue_wait_time > 200ms OR active_connections >= configured_max for 10s. Breaker action: return graceful degradation (cached response or minimal metadata) and emit structured event for routing policy.
4) Probabilistic load-shedding: implement importance-weighted shedding that maintains higher admission for requests tagged as 'interactive' or 'high-priority' and uses a sigmoid drop probability based on current cpu/utilization/queue_depth. Provide a global safety floor for logged-in enterprise customers (configurable per account).
5) Multi-region failover: add a hedged-routing module that can route to region B with read-only or degraded model variants when local capacity is saturated. Ensure KV cache affinity TTL is short to avoid stale hits after failover.
6) Kafka producer/backpressure: use a bounded producer buffer and backpressure propagation to callers; if Kafka is saturated, mark dependent routes as degraded and increment circuit-breaker failure metrics.
7) Postgres: prioritize small, short queries through a separate pool; large analytical queries are routed to async job queue.

Trade-offs and rationale:
- Hedging adds extra load; we cap hedged fraction and prefer stale/cheaper variants to reduce cost.
- Probabilistic shedding sacrifices some requests to maintain SLOs for most traffic. We favor client-visible partial results over timeouts.
- Circuit breaker thresholds tuned to avoid flapping; add hysteresis and cooldown windows.

Instrumentation and telemetry:
- New metrics: broken_out_of_pool_count, hedged_request_rate, shed_rate_by_priority, breaker_state_* , queue_wait_histogram, downstream_error_rate_by_backend.
- Dashboards: SLO overview per route, pool health, regional-hedge-effectiveness.
- Alerts: p99 latency drift > 15% vs baseline, breaker open rate > 5% for >5m, shed_rate > 25% for 10m.
